about:
# Factoruide

**A leveling guide built for you**: your character, your professions, your zones, your dungeons
and the way you play. For **WoW Forever**, **Classic Era / Hardcore** and **TBC Anniversary**.

Leveling guides follow one route written for everyone. Factoruide computes yours: it simulates
the whole playthrough with your choices (travel, fights, drops, quest and mob XP, trainers,
professions, and how strong your character gets with its gear and spells) and searches for the
fastest route to your target level, killing the mobs met on the way and grinding only a small
share of each level. The in-game addon then takes you through it step by step.

![A guide's page: its route on the map with the level reached at each stage, its play time, quests, dungeons, flights and XP](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brouznouf/factoruide/main/docs/guide.png)

## An experiment

Factoruide is experimental. A guide comes from a simulation of the game, and the simulation is
not the game: it can produce inconsistencies (a quest you cannot get, a detour that makes no
sense, a time far from yours). When you meet one, please
[open an issue](https://github.com/brouznouf/factoruide/issues) with your guide attached: the
"Share" button of its page saves it as a `.fgguide` file.

It will never replace the guides written by hand, and that is not the goal: their authors play
their route again and again, and a good one will most likely be faster. Factoruide builds a
guide of your own that holds together as a whole and gives your leveling real directions: which
zones to do, the level to reach before moving on from each, and where the XP is.

## A guide that fits you

- **Your character**: race, class and level range: start a guide at level 1, or from your
  character as it is in game. The addon records it at each logout (or at once from its page of
  the game's options: **Save the profile now**): pick it in the list of the new guide and the guide goes on from where it
  stands: its quests done are left out, those in its log are taken again when they help (as if
  never taken) and abandoned as the first step otherwise, from its position, with its
  hearthstone, flight paths, rested XP, gear, spells and professions.
- **Your professions**: two primary professions and the secondary ones, with the skill to have
  at each level from the level you take them (curves from classic guides, editable). They add no
  time to the route: the addon shows whether you are ahead or behind, and their quests are
  suggested as optional steps.
- **Your zones**: click the map to prefer the zones you like and exclude the ones you don't want
  to see again.
- **Your dungeons**: force or exclude each dungeon, do the worthwhile ones in a group, take their
  quests a few levels ahead.
- **Your quests**: search a must-have quest by name or ID (bottom of the new guide page). The guide
  includes its prerequisites and finishes the chain, even past your target level. It cannot be saved with
  a required quest missing. Each selected quest can have an inclusive minimum and/or maximum
  turn-in level, before reward XP; its prerequisites may be done earlier. Tight deadlines can
  displace optional quests.
- **Your XP buffs** (Forever): food adds 5% kill XP. Sleeping Bag adds 3% kill and quest XP
  after its quest chain is completed; enabling it includes the chain. Both buffs stay active,
  with no upkeep time; the addon warns when a buff the guide counts on is missing. Both are off by
  default. Rested XP remains finite, including when pre-grinding or catching up
  with a group in any supported edition.
- **Your travel spells**: learned Cat Form, Travel Form, Ghost Wolf and Aspect of the Cheetah
  affect walking estimates only for walks entirely outdoors without swimming; few walks currently
  qualify. In Advanced, **Assume movement talents are learned** is on by default. Cheetah needs
  no talent. Forms become available through the quests or trainers of your game version.
- **Your class spells**: quest rewards and trainer visits determine which spells are known.
  Form attacks need both the form and its learned attack rank. Imported characters use their
  recorded spells and completed quests. Without a character profile, earlier class unlocks
  are assumed known; selecting class quests does not change that starting assumption.
- **Your class quests**: the ones you want to do are kept, even when they are not the fastest.
  Missing unlocks keep their prerequisites, and known unlocks are not repeated. Druids include
  Moonglade by default.
- **Your play style**: a relaxed, normal or fast pace (time per fight, per loot, per stop), how far
  above your level you take quests and fight mobs, how much grinding you accept, flights or
  walking to save gold, finishing a zone before leaving, staying on one continent, elite quests
  solo or in a group, how crowded the server is (escorts, events and small spots fought over).
- **Your group**: level in a duo or a group with other classes: faster fights, shared XP with the
  group bonus, quest items for everyone, each class's quests and trainers.
- **Your language**: the app and the guide in 10 languages. A guide is computed once and shown in
  the app's language; the addon writes it in the language you choose in its options.

![A new guide: character, professions, play style, dungeons by level and the zones to prefer or exclude on the map](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brouznouf/factoruide/main/docs/new-guide.png)

## It adapts as you play

- The addon follows you: it advances by itself (quest accepted, objective done, quest turned in,
  flight, level reached), points the compass at the next step and compares your real time per level
  with the guide's (**Time per level** in its window).
- Ahead, behind, changed your mind about a profession or a zone? Generate the guide again from your
  character as it is now: it becomes a new version of the guide, with the difference from the previous
  one, and you choose the version its characters follow.
- The guides learn from the game: the XP and positions the addon records replace the estimates,
  and the "Contribute" page sends what your game sees to the Factoruide server (anonymous, only what
  is new, automatically if you turn it on) and lists the other tools that feed the community's quest
  databases.
- Rework a guide by hand: move, remove or add steps (a quest, the hearthstone, a flight, mobs to
  kill), the guide replayed after each change with its new time and the steps that are no longer
  possible; saved as a new version once every step holds. Or write one from scratch: "Manual
  creation" on the New guide page starts a guide with no steps from your character.
- Share a guide with a friend as a `.fgguide` file; they import it in their app.

![The characters the addon recorded, each with its level, professions and the guide it follows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brouznouf/factoruide/main/docs/characters.png)

## Getting started

1. Download the app from the [latest release](https://github.com/brouznouf/factoruide/releases/latest)
   and install it. New versions are then offered by the app at startup.
   - **Windows**: run the `_x64-setup.exe` installer. Windows may warn about an unknown publisher
     the first time (the installer is not code-signed).
   - **macOS**: open the `_aarch64.dmg` (Apple Silicon) or `_x64.dmg` (Intel) and drag the app to
     Applications. The app is not notarized by Apple, so macOS refuses to open it the first time:
     go to System Settings > Privacy & Security and click "Open Anyway", or run
     `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Factoruide.app`. Updates do not ask again.
   - **Linux** (x86_64): make the `_amd64.AppImage` executable (`chmod +x`) and run it; it updates
     itself. Or take the executable alone (`_amd64.tar.gz`), which needs WebKitGTK 4.1 installed
     (`libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0` on Debian/Ubuntu, `webkit2gtk4.1` on Fedora, `webkit2gtk-4.1` on Arch).
2. **Settings**: choose your WoW folder. Install the addon from
   [CurseForge](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/search?search=factoruide) (or your addon manager)
   and set it up in game: `/fg` opens the addon's page in the game's options (AddOns →
   Factoruide). The app warns when it is missing or too old.
3. **New guide**: pick your character, professions, zones, dungeons and play style, then start
   the generation (about 2 minutes, 6 for a thorough one, depending on the processor). The best
   starting routes are picked first, then improved in rounds where the better half goes on: their
   times go down live on the chart and the route is drawn on the map. The
   guide kept (in bold) is the best balance between play time and comfort (little grinding, few
   trips between zones), not always the very shortest.

   ![Generating a guide: the time of the guide kept going down live, and its route drawn on the map](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brouznouf/factoruide/main/docs/generation.png)
4. **Characters**: choose the guide each character follows (a guide started from a character
   follows it already), then `/reload` in game. A character follows only the guide chosen for it.
   The app writes the guides in a data addon of its own, `Factoruide_Data` (restart the game the
   first time, so that it finds the new folder).

### App updates

Published builds check for a new version at startup and offer it with its notes. To check
again, use **Check for updates** in Settings, under the version (on macOS also
**Factoruide → Check for Updates…**). Installing waits for a running generation to end.

### Building on macOS

Install Xcode Command Line Tools (`xcode-select --install`, or use a full Xcode
installation), Node.js 22 and npm, and Rust via [rustup](https://rustup.rs/).
The repository's `rust-toolchain.toml` selects the Rust version. Then, from a clone:

```sh
./scripts/build-macos.sh
open target/release/bundle/macos/Factoruide.app
```

The script installs the locked frontend dependencies, builds a native app for the
Mac running the build, and applies and verifies a local ad-hoc signature. No Apple
developer certificate or publisher updater key is needed. You can copy the app to
Applications. This is a local build, not an Apple-notarized distribution, and it
does not check for the publisher's automatic updates.

The app defaults to `/Applications/World of Warcraft`; choose another installation
in **Settings** if needed. Follow the addon and guide steps above.

Verified on Apple Silicon with WoW Forever: native app launch, character profile
import, guide generation and user-reported in-game use. Intel Macs have not been
verified.

### Building on Linux

Install WebKitGTK 4.1 and the build tools (on Debian/Ubuntu: `libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev
libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev libxdo-dev libssl-dev patchelf file build-essential`),
Node.js 22 and npm, and Rust via [rustup](https://rustup.rs/). Then, from a clone:

```sh
./scripts/build-linux.sh
./target/release/factoruide-app
```

The script builds the executable and an AppImage in `target/release/bundle/appimage`. Local
builds do not check for the publisher's automatic updates. Outside WSL, the app defaults to
Battle.net in Lutris' Wine prefix (`~/Games/battlenet/drive_c/Program Files (x86)/World of
Warcraft`); choose another folder in Settings if needed.

### In a browser

The app also builds as a website: a folder of static files where the guides are computed in
the browser (`scripts/build-web.sh`). The browser cannot reach the game's folder: characters
come from the game with **Export my character** in the addon's options (pasted in New guide), and
guides go to it with **Import a guide…** (the text a guide's Export gives). See
[web/README.md](https://github.com/brouznouf/factoruide/blob/main/web/README.md).

### Releases

`scripts/release.sh X.Y.Z` tags main and pushes the tag; `.github/workflows/release.yml` then
publishes everything under that one version: the desktop apps (GitHub release and updates), the
web app (Cloudflare Pages) and the addons. An addon is published (CurseForge, Wago and a zip in
the release) only when it changed since the last release: the script gives it the new version
first, and the apps built from the tag ask for that version at least. Each addon has its own
`CHANGELOG.md` (what changes for players, its changelog on CurseForge and Wago): new lines go under
Unreleased, which the script dates with the version, and it stops when a changed addon has none.
`scripts/publish-addons.sh X.Y.Z [addon] [beta|alpha|release]` publishes the addons of main
outside a release, to try them. A guide made by an older
app stays readable by a newer addon: `addon/tests/guides` keeps one guide per release, and the
addon's tests follow each of them.

## In game: the addon

The addon comes in two parts, installed from CurseForge: **Factoruide_Profile** records your
character and what the game shows (profile, collector below; **Export my character** gives it to
the web app), **Factoruide_Guide** shows the guide and everything around it. Each can go without
the other: another addon can show your guides. `/fg` (or `/factoruide`) opens the addon's page in
the game's options (AddOns → Factoruide): the character (**Export my character**, **Save the
profile now**) and the guides (choose the one each character follows, start over, import, delete),
then a page per group of settings and an Advanced page (the recordings). What you do while
playing is on the guide's buttons and in the game's key bindings (Factoruide section): next and
previous step, mark a step done, undo the last mark, next spot, full or minimal guide, show or
hide the guide or all the addon's windows, time per level, quest item, the options.
On WoW Forever with [Polestar](https://github.com/fitzforge/polestar) installed, the app also
writes your guides as a Polestar guide pack (Factoruide_Polestar; the web app downloads it). In Polestar, choose Factoruide
under "Suggest guides from" on the "Community guides" page: it offers each character the guide of
its race and class. A guide's **Export → Polestar: addon** adds that guide alone to a
`Factoruide_Polestar` folder you choose (or the folder itself when it is the pack), keeping the
pack's other guides, with no step limit: copy the folder into `Interface\AddOns` and restart the
game (the web app downloads the pack with that guide). **Export → Polestar: import text** gives
the text to paste on Polestar's Import page (`/polestar import`), for guides of up to 60 steps.

- Guide: follows the guide chosen for the character (in the options' guides; the only one of
  its race and class by itself) and advances by itself; previous and next step, start over on the
  guide's buttons, mark a step done with a right click or a key binding. Two modes: full (a card with the current tasks, the next steps and
  the talent to learn) or minimal (a strip at the top of the screen, the next steps on
  mouse-over); a button or a key binding switches. Mobs living in several places: the compass
  moves on to another place when nothing is found at one (**Next spot**, a key binding, at once), and the world
  map shows them all.
- **Show or hide the guide** (a key binding, or the setting) shows or hides the guide only;
  **Show or hide all the addon's windows** (a key binding) hides all of its windows and marks
  (guide, compass, quest panel, quest item button, map pins and waypoint, the
  upgrade line of item tooltips, safety alerts) and the same key brings them back as they were.
  For the session only: progress is kept and the automation goes on; pressed in combat, it
  applies when the fight ends.
- Windows move by dragging them anywhere; **Lock the windows** (a setting) locks them. Size:
  Ctrl + mouse wheel over a window, or the window size setting.
- The compass: drag it to move it, Ctrl + mouse wheel over it for its own size, drag its ends for
  its width (kept per character); a setting hides or shows it, **Compass back to the top** puts it
  back at the top of the screen at its first size. In minimal mode it sits on the strip and moves
  with it.
- Helpers: a compass bar at the top of the screen with the step to go to (it stands out, with its
  distance, even behind you), the other current tasks, the quests to pick up close by, the next
  turn-in and the places you choose in the app (your class trainer, your professions' trainers,
  flight masters, innkeepers, vendors, bankers, mailboxes...; mouse over: what and how far; click:
  go there). A green mark shows the way the guide planned on foot, around cliffs and water,
  orange when you stray from it; the same way is dotted on the world map and the minimap (an
  option), and a 3D arrow can follow it next to the compass (another option). When the NPC to go
  to shows its nameplate, a mark sits right above its head. On WoW Forever, [Shortest Path Forever](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/shortest-path-forever)
  (when installed) gets the place to go to and guides you there with flights, boats and its own
  map lines; a click on the compass changes its destination. Targeting macro "FG Cible"
  (**Pick up the target macro**), quest item button (key binding in the game's
  key bindings, Factoruide section), the step's flight taken automatically, next steps numbered on
  the world map.
- Vendors: sells gray items, repairs, buys food, water and ammunition for your level (disabled by
  default; hold Shift when opening to skip everything).
- Gear and talents: the quest reward the guide planned (the route counts on wearing it), upgrades
  in tooltips and on quest rewards, the recommended talent in the guide. At the class trainer,
  only the spells that matter for leveling are bought.
- Quest panel: one line per quest in the guide's order, tabs for the guide's professions and
  reputation goals, and the items to keep for its quests (cloth, meat…) with how many are in the
  bags and the bank (read at each visit; at the bank it says what to take and what can stay).
- Group and safety: party members' progress in the quest panel, alerts on elite or high-level
  targets and low health, elite objectives flagged in the guide.
- Profile: what the app needs to start a guide from your character (level, XP, quests done and in
  the log, position, hearthstone, flight paths seen on flight maps, professions, gear, spells),
  kept up to date every minute and at logout; **Save the profile now** writes it to disk at once
  (the interface reloads).
- Collector: records what you see (givers, positions, XP received) for the next guides; its
  events, debug messages and clearing are in the window's Advanced section.

## How it works

How the optimized route is computed: [ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/brouznouf/factoruide/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md).

## License

The code is under the MIT license ([LICENSE](https://github.com/brouznouf/factoruide/blob/main/LICENSE)). The quest databases (`data/`) are under
GPL-3.0, the license of the server data they include ([data/LICENSE](https://github.com/brouznouf/factoruide/blob/main/data/LICENSE));
their sources and the terms of each are listed in [NOTICE.md](https://github.com/brouznouf/factoruide/blob/main/NOTICE.md).
changelog:
# Changelog

Each version's tag message (`scripts/release.sh`), shown in the app's update prompt, is kept short: a link to this file.

Writing an entry: one short line per change, saying what the player sees or gets (not how it works inside), grouped under App, Guides, Addon and WoW data. Numbers and examples only when they tell the change better than words; details go to the commit.

An addon change also goes, in the same words, under Unreleased in that addon's own `addon/<addon>/CHANGELOG.md`: its changelog on CurseForge and Wago.

## Unreleased

### App

- A character made in the app above level 10 starts at its capital's inn, its hearthstone bound there, instead of its starting zone; Start from chooses another inn.
- A character the addon could not fully read in game says which parts (done quests, professions...) and how to read them again.

### Guides

- WoW Forever: loot is sold to merchants players have seen in the game rather than to NPCs the data only guesses sell, such as a Kor'kron Elite guard in Orgrimmar.
- WoW Forever: The Darkmoon Faire quest, offered by the Faire's barker, is no longer in the guides, like the Faire's other quests: the Faire is only there one week a month.
- Cloth donations to the cities (A Donation of Wool and the others) are no longer in the guides: the cloth is better used by professions. A new advanced setting, Cloth donations to the cities, brings them back.

### Addon

- The target macro names the monsters and NPCs in the game's language, whatever the guide's language.
- Your profile no longer loses its done quests, professions or quest log after a loading screen.

### WoW data

- WoW Forever: the latest quest data, with named monsters and quest givers at the places they really stand instead of dozens of sightings, and more quests seen in game by players.
- WoW Forever: more quest and creature names right in Spanish and French, and drop rates measured in game by players.
- WoW Forever: Krol'dok Moulding for the Horde, begun by the mould Tunk drops in Krol'dok Stronghold.
- WoW Forever: more Mount Hyjal quests in the guides (A Thorn in the Paw, Praise and Ends Meet), The Darkreaver Menace for Alliance shamans only, and the newest quests of the client.
- WoW Forever: Just Compensation, Anthion's Parting Words and the epic riding quests now have their giver, the Magram clan quests of Desolace for the Horde only, and more Alterac Valley and Warsong Gulch names in French and Spanish.
- WoW Forever: In Demand - Plague Records, In Demand - Titan Relics and Ott's Finest Work now have their giver, more quest and object names in French, German and Spanish, and fresher drop rates measured in game by players.
- WoW Forever: nine quest chains no longer broken, Your First Horse, Swift as the Wind, Scalebeard and Bait the Beast in the guides, creatures at fresher places, and more names in Spanish, French, Russian and Korean.
- WoW Forever: the latest quest data and client, more Just Compensation, Anthion's Parting Words and epic riding quests available, and thousands more names translated, in French, Spanish, German and Korean above all.

## 0.21.0 (2026-11-16)

Kills count for every quest that wants them, trainers that teach the rank you need, guides exported as a Polestar addon, and more WoW Forever quests in the guides.

### App

- WoW Forever: **Export → Polestar: addon** puts one guide, however long, into the Factoruide_Polestar addon folder you choose, next to the guides already there, ready to copy into the game. It replaces the export to Polestar's .guide format, which the game could not load.

### Guides

- Two new settings for quest items that drop rarely: a minimum drop rate under which their quest is left out, and a weight that makes the guide avoid them the rarer they drop. Both are off by default.
- Monsters count at the average of their level range, and a camp of several kinds at the average of them all rather than its lowest: fewer camps turn out tougher than the guide planned.
- Kills count for every quest in your log that wants them, as in the game (the scarlet warriors to kill also drop the rings to bring back): guide times and levels are closer to what you play, and quests on the same monsters are done together.
- Profession trainer visits go to trainers that teach the rank you need: Expert Cooking, Fishing and First Aid come from their book, bought from its vendor, and crafting trainers teach the rank below their title (an Expert Blacksmith teaches Journeyman).
- WoW Forever, Riverglades: notes on where the lost horse waits and its ambushes, on Ghostmaw's path down the river, and on the way into the caves under Sunnyglade.

### Addon

- WoW Forever: a click on a quest in the quest panel makes the game track it, as from the game's own tracker, and a click on the step already shown sets the game's waypoint again.
- WoW Forever: the items a quest needs are bought at the merchant, as on Classic and TBC, and the low health alert in combat and the items to keep at login no longer run into errors.

### WoW data

- WoW Forever: the latest quest data, with the Shen'dralas chains in their order, quest givers corrected in Stranglethorn Vale, Riverglades and Desolace, and more names checked in Spanish, Korean and Russian.
- WoW Forever: Riverglades places measured in game (the Foreman's Crate, the lost horse, Ghostmaw along the river), with the horse escort and What We Lost back in the guides, more quest XP measured by players, and more names checked in Spanish, French, German and Korean.
- WoW Forever: 75 more quests with their objectives, known from the game itself (In Memoriam, Get the Goods, Upstream Contamination...), back in the guides.

## 0.20.0 (2026-11-13)

WoW Forever's new dungeons and reputation quests in the guides, class quests always planned, and fixes from players' reports.

### App

- A new version of a guide (set up again, computed again, edited or imported) is the one sent to the game, even after an older one was chosen with "Use this version".
- A new guide's name filled in from its character follows the level to reach: lowering it to 40 no longer leaves "Name 25-60" on the guide, its file and its Polestar title.

### Guides

- Class quests are always in the guide, started as soon as they can be: the dwarf shaman's and the Horde rogues' guides could not be made.
- Townsfolk the game data knows little of no longer pass for monsters guarding the quests around them, nor do creatures far above the quest's level: the guides keep those quests (Southshore, Tarren Mill, Lakeshire, Goldshire, and many in Feralas and Winterspring).
- Skyborne guides no longer take the portal from Stormwind to Dalaran, removed from the game; the one from Dalaran to Stormwind is taken for Welcome to Azeroth only.
- Quests asking for a reputation are planned: the guide first kills the creatures whose kills give it ("Kill 50 Gelkis Mauler for reputation with Magram Clan Centaur"). A new setting picks Desolace's centaur clan: Auto, Magram or Gelkis.

### Addon

- Escort and event quests are never accepted automatically, nor joined when a party member starts them: in a group, everyone has time to turn in the quest before.

### WoW data

- The latest quest data: more quests known in Riverglades, Shen'dralas and Stranglethorn Vale, and Riverglades chains completed with their missing objectives.
- The Drowned City, a dungeon of levels 35-40 off Stranglethorn Vale: its quests are done during its run (the four tablets of The Drowned City, the Saltseers, Var'Taka).
- Krol'dok Stronghold (40-45), Alcaz Prison (48-53) and Blackmaw Hold (55-60), WoW Forever's other new dungeons: their quests are done during their run.
- The Magram and Gelkis quests of the Valley of Bones ask for Honored with their clan, with their objectives.
- WoW Forever: Skyborne shamans of the Horde get Storm, Earth, and Fire and the rest of its chain.

## 0.19.0 (2026-11-12)

Quest notes in the guides, with tips and warnings on tricky quests, and fixes to the quest data from players' reports.

### App

- Steps show how their quest is taken (an item, an object, a mob's drop, an event) or their objective done, and a mark when a note tells more about the quest.

### Guides

- Quest notes: tips and warnings about a quest (good to know, watch out, must read), written in the guide's language; Jungle Secrets says how to get it from Private Thorsen.

### Addon

- Steps show how their quest is taken or their objective done, and a yellow, orange or red mark when a note tells more about the quest; the step's tooltip lists the notes.
- A quest handed in far ahead of the guide no longer marks the merchants, trainers and flight masters before it as visited.

### WoW data

- WoW Forever: the latest quest data, with 115 more quests a guide can take (most in Riverglades and Desolace), the Duskwood Missions left out again, and more names checked in Spanish and Korean.
- About 200 more NPCs who walk a road (Gann Stonespire, the Defias Messenger, Duskwing...) show where to find them along their path.
- Classic Era: hundreds of quest objectives shown in English again, not French.
- Fixes from players' reports: rare drops and long respawns counted as players see them (Thick Yeti Hide, Book: The Powers Below, Zzarc' Vul...), quests that need an event or a rare item first (Assassin's Contract, Arena Master, Dagun, Gahz'rilla), the teleport up to Xylem's tower, and a few WoW Forever chains.

## 0.18.0 (2026-11-11)

WoW Forever's guide map on one seamless map of Azeroth, and the latest WoW Forever data.

### App

- The web app no longer runs out of memory while making a guide, nor after making a few.
- A web app built on Windows includes its game databases and map images.
- The guide map zooms in further, draws only the steps from the current one (a slider sets how many of the zone's), and arrows show which way the route goes.
- WoW Forever: the guide map is one seamless map of Azeroth, every zone's art blended into its neighbours, the game's minimap showing through as you zoom in; Zephras Isle floats in its frame between the continents.
- Zoomed in on the guide map, caves, Ironforge and Undercity show as the game's minimap draws them inside.
- The zone maps no longer miss pieces of their explored areas (Duskwood's Twilight Grove, among others).

### Guides

- A forced dungeon is run even when it has no quest for your character (Shadowfang Keep for the Alliance).
- Loot is no longer sold to warlock-only demon trainers in a guide for another class.
- The quests inside a dungeon are finished before leaving for another forced dungeon.

### Addon

- No more blocked-action errors from the quest panel during a fight; its layout catches up afterwards.
- Guides pasted on Windows no longer fail to import on large numbers.

### WoW data

## 0.16.0 (2026-11-07)

A guide for one dungeon from your character, dungeons as zones with their steps on their floor maps, every quest of a dungeon forced with its quests, and the fixes of your reports (GitHub #97 to #125).

### App

- A Dungeon tab: pick a character and a dungeon for a short guide of every quest of that dungeon, with the quests leading to them, and nothing else. A character below the level its quests need gets a warning.
- The steps inside a dungeon are a block of their own on the guide page, shown on the map of the dungeon's floor they are on (Classic and WoW Forever dungeons, from the game's own dungeon maps).
- The first guide of a game version no longer fails now and then because another command removed its data while unpacking it.
- A settings change made while the addon installs, or while a character is added back or forgotten, is no longer lost.
- A dungeon quest with one objective inside shows its name in the guide ("An Ancient Grudge: Faldrim Anvilmar"), not the dungeon's ("The Hall of Thanes: Faldrim Anvilmar").

### Guides

- A dungeon's quests are steps inside it: taken from a boss's drop or a giver inside, objectives and hand-ins, each where it is done, the dungeon entered once (its run's time and mobs counted then). Guides made before get those steps when opened.
- After a quest at an NPC who walks around, the level checkpoint's arrow points at the checkpoint, not along the NPC's path.
- A guide text with a control character or a character name with an unusual letter is written into the data addon as the game reads it, not as stray letters.
- "On the way: buy ... at the auction house" comes before the flight, boat or zeppelin that leaves the city, not after it (GitHub #115).
- WoW Forever: the Orc mage takes the Undercity mage quests (Investigate the Alchemist Shop, Spellfire Robes, Speak with Deino...), the Troll warlock the Voidwalker's Creature of the Void and The Binding, and the High Order Skyborne mage and druid the Human, Gnome and Night Elf quests of their sides, instead of leaving them out of the guide (GitHub #111, #114).
- Class quests: the guide takes one version of each (the Skyborne shaman's two Call of Fire chains, the human priest's Divine Grace, the warlocks' demons by race...) instead of all of them, and a class quest no version of which can be planned is reported. The races of the class quests follow the quests' pages (the troll warlock gets its Voidwalker and Incubus, Piercing the Veil is the orc and undead warlocks') (GitHub #110, #111, #112, #114).
- Web app: when the backend stops, the message carries what it wrote on its error output (a panic's place and reason) and the error's own message, so that a report says why (GitHub #109).
- A must-have quest asked at a minimum level ("complete it at level 18") has its dungeon run from that level, instead of before it and the hand-in after (GitHub #108).
- WoW Forever: Lost in the Thicket Things (Excavation Site: Wetlands) is ended to Ardin Grassman inside the dungeon, who gives Heartwoven to take back to Caitlin Grassman in Menethil Harbor: the guide runs the dungeon once for both (GitHub #107).
- A quest the guide takes and never hands in is grinding in all but name: the time of its kills counts as grinding, in the planner's score and against the grind limit. Guides no longer end on a many-hour step for a quest they never hand in, nor keep quests only for their kills (GitHub #117, #124).
- A must-have quest (one you ask for, or a class quest the guide requires) is done while the game shows it yellow (orange with the risky profile) or green, not before and not once it is gray; a guide that cannot do it in time is refused instead of doing it levels late: the warlock's Felhunter comes by level 37 and the Felsteed by 50 instead of 44-51 (GitHub #113). Guides already made are not refused for it.
- A quest started by an item found in a dungeon's object is planned with the run and taken in it: WoW Forever's The Treaty of Understanding, from the Hall of Thanes.
- Dungeons run above their monsters' level: the level-60 dungeons are run at 60 instead of leaving the guide impossible to make (GitHub #99).
- "Profession trainer stops" option (under the professions of a player of the new guide, off by default): with professions, the route goes to the trainer to learn each profession and, before the skill reaches the cap of its rank, each next rank. A trainer near the route is a detour, a far one a trip, both counted in the route's time; a rank no trainer teaches has no stop (GitHub #106).
- A dungeon forced with its quests does all of them: a delivery filed under a dungeon ("Speak with Nara Wildmane") no longer asks for a run of its own, a breadcrumb the guide needs comes before the quest it leads to, a quest taken inside a dungeon is no longer held back by the creatures at its entrance, and the quest unlocking one of the dungeon's is done before its last level (GitHub #125).
- WoW Forever: the rogue quests of C's dead drop near Pyrewood (The Horn of Xelthos, The Eye of Bhossca) can be in a guide: the infiltration alone at the dungeon's entrance, then the letter at a capital's mailbox and the reward at the dead drop (GitHub #125).
- "Buy at the auction house" option (advanced settings, off by default): the items a quest asks for that nothing else gives, made by a profession like Rough Dynamite, are bought at the nearest auction house instead of leaving the quest out (GitHub #97).
